about: Big Green is the New York rye of Hollerhorn Distilling, a family farm distillery in the hills above Naples, at the southern tip of Canandaigua Lake. Karl and Melissa Neubauer opened in 2018 in a building Karl raised himself from reclaimed barn timber; after a fire in 2022 they rebuilt, and the barrels that survived went on aging. Karl is the only distiller, and nearly everything he ferments is grown within about forty miles.

It carries the Empire Rye designation, New York’s own standard: at least 75% New York-grown rye, made at a single New York distillery and aged at least two years in new charred oak. Hollerhorn uses heirloom grains from the Finger Lakes and the Naples Valley, ferments and distills them in Naples, and fills a mix of barrels, some from a Hudson Valley cooperage. It is barreled at low proof and bottled without filtration or added water. The distillery’s notes describe a rich, oily rye with caramel, cinnamon spice (they compare it to Big Red chewing gum), a long sweet-spice finish and a touch of vanilla crème brûlée.
facts: At least 75% New York-grown rye; 100% New York heirloom grains
New charred oak, mixed barrels incl. Hudson Valley cooperage
Varies by batch (one release 98.2 proof / 49.1% ABV)
title: Hollerhorn Distilling “Big Green” Empire Rye
